Drop rows or columns that are empty in selected columns

Source: R/drop_empty.R
drop_empty_rows.Rd

drop_empty_rows() removes a row only when every selected column is missing in that row. Other columns, such as identifiers, are kept but do not influence the decision. drop_empty_cols() removes only selected columns that are entirely missing.

Usage

drop_empty_rows(data, ..., blank = FALSE)

drop_empty_cols(data, ..., blank = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

...

Columns to inspect, using tidyselect syntax: bare names, ranges, starts_with(), where(is.numeric), or all_of(names). With no selection, all columns are inspected. Columns cannot be renamed.

blank

Also consider empty strings and whitespace-only strings empty? Default FALSE. Applies to character and factor columns; retained values are never trimmed or changed. Zero and FALSE are not empty.

Value

The input data with empty rows or selected empty columns removed.

Details

Missingness follows is.na(), including NaN. With blank = TRUE, whitespace includes spaces, tabs, line breaks, and Unicode separators. List columns use is.na() on each list element; their contents are not recursively inspected. Matrix and data-frame columns must be excluded from the selection.

An empty selection returns the input unchanged. An input with zero rows keeps its columns, preserving its schema. An input with zero columns keeps its rows. Both functions preserve column types and row order. Decisions use the entire input, including for grouped data. Remaining grouping columns are preserved; removing a grouping column updates the grouping metadata.

To remove both empty rows and empty columns, call drop_empty_rows() followed by drop_empty_cols().

Examples

df <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:3,
  score_a = c(1, NA, NA),
  score_b = c(NA_real_, NA_real_, NA_real_),
  comment = c("ok", "", "  ")
)
drop_empty_rows(df, starts_with("score_"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>      id score_a score_b comment
#>   <int>   <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1     1       1      NA ok     
drop_empty_rows(df, comment, blank = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>      id score_a score_b comment
#>   <int>   <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1     1       1      NA ok     
drop_empty_cols(df, where(is.numeric))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>      id score_a comment
#>   <int>   <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1     1       1 "ok"   
#> 2     2      NA ""     
#> 3     3      NA "  "   
df |> drop_empty_rows(starts_with("score_")) |> drop_empty_cols()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>      id score_a comment
#>   <int>   <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1     1       1 ok
